newsitem.title: UK: Diesel, gasoline firm in Med, fuel oil held back.
newsitem.headline: Diesel, gasoline firm in Med, fuel oil held back.

text.p: Diesel and gasoline prices firmed in the Med on better demand on Tuesday but fuel oil was weighed down by an oversupply of Russian material, traders said.
An open arbitrage to northern Europe firmed low sulphur diesel, with a 50,000 tonne cargo heard sold at high fob EN590 quotes +$1.50-$2 a tonne fob Italy to a north European refiner
A one percent sulphur cargo was sold on Monday out of Italy at a slight discount to fob high quotes. But the market for Russian and Italian heating oil remained subdued.
Gasoline was firm amid fairly good demand and tight supply, traders said.
Demand out of Turkey, Greece and Lebanon was supportive.
Turkey was reported to have bought 27,000 tonnes of gasoline from Total at a discount of $17.12 per tonne to fob Mediterranean Italy quotations to be delivered May 24-26.
Spot premium unleaded prices were assessed at fob quotes +$2.50, and unleaded material at around fob quotes +$2.0.
Naphtha remained fairly sloppy for promptish material, while June was looking more bullish on expectations of higher demand.
Russian fuel oil cargoes were weighing heavily on the Med market, with buyers scarce and the summer waterways export programme in full swing.
"There are M-40s all over the place -- on the water, getting on the water, loading in 5 days," said one trader.
"You can argue they should have high premiums because the quotes are low compared to crude but prompt supply is really heavy, so refiners should be able to get low numbers," he added.
Cracked fuel markets were suffering from seller/buyer quality mismatches, with little seen done. Prices were notionally steady to $1 lower.
Low sulphur was supported by higher European swaps numbers.
